t: North Korea Tests Two Types of Submarine-Launched Strategic Cruise Missiles
d: North Korea’s Missile Administration test-fired two types of submarine-launched strategic cruise missiles in the East Sea of Korea on October 14, KCNA reported.

t: ASEAN Puts Strategic Autonomy and Engagement Over Bloc Politics — Secretary-General
d: ASEAN Secretary-General Kao Kim Hourn told Sputnik that the bloc intends to keep strengthening its own mechanisms while maintaining relations with partners both inside and outside the region.

t: Starshield Restrictions Disrupt Ukrainian Drone Strikes as Musk Points to Pentagon
d: New Starshield speed restrictions have disrupted Ukrainian drone operations, forcing some planned strikes to be cancelled and causing communication losses lasting 10–20 seconds, The Telegraph reported.

t: Russian Armed Forces Struck Izmail Port Military Infrastructure
d: During an overnight strike, the Russian military hit infrastructure at the port of Izmail in the Odessa Region that was used by the armed forces of Ukraine, the Russian Defense Ministry said in a statement.

t: Trump Open to Economic Cooperation With Russia After Peace Achieved in Ukraine - Reports
d: US President Donald Trump is open to economic cooperation between the US and Russia after the end of the Ukraine conflict, The Wall Street Journal newspaper reported, citing the Trump administration.

t: Ukraine Forced to Cancel Drone Missions Following Starlink Slowdown - Reports
d: Ukraine is forced to cancel missions involving drones due to a slowdown in the Starlink satellite communication system, The Telegraph reported, citing Ukrainian assault troops.

t: Swedish Citizen Plotting Sabotage at Russia Military Objects Detained in Pskov Region - FSB
d: The Russian Federal Security Service (FSB) said on Thursday that it had detained a Swedish citizen in the Pskov Region who planned acts of sabotage at military facilities under the pretext of joining the Russian armed forces.

t: Russia Sources Over 84% of Oil, Gas Equipment Domestically - Industry Ministry
d: The share of Russian-made oil and gas equipment in the domestic market has exceeded 84%, Russian Deputy Industry and Trade Minister Mikhail Ivanov said at the Russian Energy Week on Thursday.

d: North Korea suspects Japanese militarists of seeking to build a nuclear weapon with the help of the United States under the pretext of developing nuclear-powered submarines, the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) reported on Thursday…

t: Russian Oil Firms Ready to Start Diesel Fuel Exports, Procedures to Take 2-3 Weeks - Deputy PM
d: Russian oil companies are ready to start exporting diesel fuel, and all the necessary procedures will take two to three weeks, Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said on Thursday.

t: Russia Liberates Nefedovka, Chernoye in Kharkov Region
d: The Russian armed forces have liberated the settlements of Nefedovka and Chernoye in the Kharkov region, the Russian Defense Ministry said on Thursday.

t: Russian Energy Ministry Says Expects Slight Decline in Coal Output in Country in 2026
d: The Russian Energy Ministry expects a slight decline in coal production in the country in 2026 to 430 million tonnes from 434 million in 2025, Russian Deputy Energy Minister Dmitry Islamov said.

t: US Shipping Regulator Proposes $200,000 Fee on Spanish Ships
d: The US Federal Maritime Commission has proposed introducing a $200,000 fee for Spanish vessels entering US ports and restricting imports of Spanish goods in response to the closure of ports to US-flagged ships.

t: Venezuela May Hike Oil Output By 200,000 Barrels Per Day in One Year - Chilean Ex-Minister
d: Venezuela may increase oil production by up to 200,000 barrels per day over the coming year under favorable conditions, former Chilean Energy Minister Ricardo Raineri told Sputnik.

t: US Efforts to Resolve Ukrainian Crisis Thwarted by Ukraine's Unwillingness to Seek Peace - Kremlin
d: Ukraine continues to strike targets in the Russian energy sector, contradicting the peace efforts of the United States, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Thursday.

t: Russia to Respond to Ukraine's Attacks on Oil Refineries, Logistics, Energy Facilities - Putin
d: Russia will respond to Ukraine's attacks on its oil refineries, logistics and energy facilities, there was no need for Ukraine to start them in the first place, Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Thursday.
